verified.name: Sidebar-header entity switcher (the shadcn TeamSwitcher shape)
verified.what: Minor unverified specifics: the exact >7-org threshold for the 210px ScrollArea cap, the precise 'md:hidden md:group-hover:block' class string, and the 'introduced Mar 2026 / last touched Aug 2026' dates for Supabase were not confirmed from the fetched source (the conditional height and hover reveal exist, but thresholds/classes/dates should be stated loosely). Also note in shadcn's collapsed rail the lg button gets p-0 while the generic collapsed button rule applies size-8 + p-2, so the tile survives by the sidebar's overflow-hidden rather than a dedicated per-button clip.
verified.products: shadcn/ui sidebar-07 block (registry new-york-v4, 2024–2026); Supabase Studio OrgSelector + ProjectBranchSelectorTrigger (mobile nav, introduced Mar 2026, last touched Aug 2026); Notion (workspace name 'at the top left of your Notion window'); Linear ('click your workspace name in the upper-left corner'); Slack desktop ('click on your workspace icon in the top left'); Figma file browser ('click your name at the top-left').
verified.tradeoff: Good: the current org is always on screen and reads as the root of the nav tree; a single component pattern already exists in shadcn so the shell gets it for free; the menu width equals the trigger so it looks anchored; keyboard shortcuts ⌘1..n are cheap to add. Bad: the block only models one level (team) — tripline's org > project > environment and runsheet's org > team/service have to go somewhere else (Supabase solved this by putting project+branch in a second lg button directly under the org button); in the 48px rail only the tile is visible so the org name needs a tooltip; a plain DropdownMenu does not scale past ~7 orgs without switching to a Command/popover with search (Supabase does); nothing in the block shows role, pending invitations or sign-out, so you must borrow those from nav-user or another pattern.

verified.name: Top-bar breadcrumb scope chain (org / project / env as switchable crumbs)
verified.what: Minor overreaches: (1) Supabase's header is not documented as 'sticky' — it is a non-scrolling flex header (shrink-0, border-b) inside the layout, and the crumb chain only shows on desktop (hidden below md; a separate mobile header exists). (2) The crumbs are not arbitrary 'org / project / env' — Supabase's third crumb is a Branch (BranchDropdown), not a generic environment; the org crumb only renders when a slug/project route is active, and the whole chain is gated behind IS_PLATFORM (self-hosted Studio shows a plain project name, no switcher). (3) Vercel's and Stripe's docs only establish a top-left switcher; the docs do not describe the 'crumb-per-scope with per-crumb link+chevron' anatomy for Vercel, and Stripe's is a single account picker (org/account/sandbox in one menu), not a breadcrumb chain. (4) Stripe's menu item is documented as 'New account', not 'Create new account'; the 'in-org vs outside-org choice' comes from the orgs docs, not the multiple-accounts page. (5) Project-menu 'New project' is feature-flagged (projects:create), like the org one.
verified.products: Supabase Studio desktop header (LayoutHeader + OrganizationDropdown/ProjectDropdown/BranchDropdown, 2024–2026); Vercel dashboard (team switcher top-left of nav bar; personal accounts converted to teams 2024-01); Stripe Dashboard account picker (upper-left, with Organisations and Sandboxes, 2024–2026).
verified.tradeoff: Good: maps 1:1 onto tripline's org > project > environment and runsheet's org > team/service — each level gets its own trigger, its own search and its own create action; the current path is legible at a glance; the Link-plus-chevron split means one click navigates and the other switches; plan/partner/usage badges attach naturally to the crumb they belong to. Bad: it competes with your existing page breadcrumbs in the sticky action bar (Supabase's own 'SidebarBreadcrumb' is a separate, non-switching component for that reason); it consumes horizontal space, so Supabase hides the org name below md and collapses the whole thing into a Sheet on mobile; the org popover is small, so account-level items (settings, invitations, sign-out) need a second home (Vercel: avatar top-right); the switchers vanish on routes with no org context, which is exactly the platform-staff 'all orgs' view you need for latchkey.

verified.name: Avatar-only rail button with a nested org menu (Sentry new navigation)
verified.what: Minor overstatements only: (1) 'aria-label ... no name, no chevron' is inferred from AvatarButton usage, not an explicit statement — accurate in effect. (2) The user AvatarButton's aria-label is the user's email, not a fixed string. (3) The org-dropdown wrapper also has a hideCurrentOrganizationLinks prop that can suppress the five per-org links entirely. (4) 'still active Sep 2026' is supported only by the file being present on master today, not by a changelog. (5) Slack's '2023 redesign onward' dating is not stated in the cited help articles.
verified.products: Sentry new navigation (static/app/views/navigation/primary/organizationDropdown.tsx and userDropdown.tsx, renamed into place Mar 2026, still active Sep 2026); Slack desktop workspace rail (2023 redesign onward).
verified.tradeoff: Good: works at 48px with no special collapsed state because the trigger is already avatar-only; cleanly separates org identity (top) from person identity (bottom, with Sign Out); role-gated menu items are a ready-made model for owner/admin/member/viewer and for a staff-only 'Admin' entry; the inactive-org group with a status tip is a good precedent for suspended tenants. Bad: the org name is never visible in the rail, so users rely on the avatar/letter alone (Sentry compensates with an 'N Projects' line only once the menu is open); switching is two levels deep (menu → submenu), which is slower than a flat list; a nested submenu is awkward on touch, hence Sentry's separate mobile layout; there is no search, so it assumes a handful of orgs, not a platform-staff view of every org; project/environment scope is not in this menu at all — Sentry puts it in a page-level filter bar.

verified.name: Identity-first switching from the account menu or a dashboard context switcher
verified.what: Identity-first switching from the account menu is documented for GitHub (dashboard-only 'Switch dashboard context' username dropdown; elsewhere orgs are reached via profile picture > Organizations) and Datadog (hover the account menu at the bottom of the left nav, or Personal Settings > Organizations). Figma is a two-tier design: the name-at-top-left menu switches accounts only, while org/team switching uses a separate dropdown next to the organization name on Org/Enterprise plans. Cloudflare docs only say 'select your account' after login and do not describe where or how the switcher is presented, so it should be cited as unverified rather than as an example of the pattern.
verified.products: GitHub (global nav from Oct 2023; docs current 2026); Datadog (multi-org docs, 2025–26); Figma file browser (2024–26); Cloudflare dashboard (2025–26, doc evidence only for the 'select your account' step).
verified.tradeoff: Good: fits the case where the person, not the org, is the stable thing — several orgs at different roles, several emails, or platform staff who see every org; keeps the sidebar header free for product nav; Datadog's bottom-left account menu already contains sign-out and personal settings, so one menu covers identity, org switch and exit. Bad: discoverability is poor (GitHub needs two different switchers — dashboard vs profile menu — and documents both); the current org is often not visible at all, which is dangerous for an error tracker or an IdP admin console where acting in the wrong tenant matters; hover-to-open (Datadog) and 'select your account' landing pages (Cloudflare) add steps; none of these carry per-org role or plan in the trigger.

verified.name: Multi-account grouped switcher with join/create and pending-invite count
verified.what: Multi-account grouped switcher with join/create and pending-invite count. Notion: the switcher "will display all the workspaces associated with your email address", grouped per signed-in account; each account row has a "•••" menu offering "Join or create workspace" and "Log out" (that account only); footer offers "Add another account", "Settings", and "Log out all"; desktop shortcut ctrl+shift+# jumps to the #-th workspace in the list. Linear: click the workspace name top-left, hover "Switch workspace" for every workspace across added emails plus "Create or join a workspace"; a number next to "Create or join a workspace" signals a pending invite; "Add account" is under your email in the upper-right of the join screen; shortcut O then W; signing out of a workspace signs out all sessions. Slack: click the workspace icon top-left (not a name) to list "all the workspaces you're signed in to"; "Add a workspace" → "Sign in to another workspace"; mobile: swipe right from Home. Figma: click your name top-left in the file browser to pick an account or "Add account" (the cited page does not describe a separate org/team dropdown).
verified.products: Notion (help current 2026); Linear (docs current 2026); Slack desktop and mobile; Figma file browser.
verified.tradeoff: Good: this is the only family that models 'a person can belong to several orgs and may have pending invitations' explicitly — the invite count badge on 'Create or join' and the per-account log-out are directly reusable; grouping by email is the right shape when sign-in is passwordless and a person may hold multiple identities; numbered shortcuts make frequent switching fast. Bad: the identity grouping adds vertical bulk and is redundant when latchkey issues a single session; nested 'Switch workspace' submenus (Linear) push the actual org list one level down; none of these show role/plan per org in the list, and none address a staff 'all orgs' mode — you would add a separate section; the trigger itself carries no sub-scope (project/env), so it pairs best with crumbs in the page action bar.

verified.name: Status-bearing trigger anatomy: secondary line, badges, selected-check and create/all-orgs escape hatches
verified.what: Minor corrections: Supabase's preview-branch colour is text-foreground-lighter (not 'muted'); the 'Exceeding usage limits' badge only renders for orgs with usage billing disabled (free / spend-capped) and lives in the layout header, not on the org trigger itself. Stripe sandbox banner and Vercel plan-based teams were not verified from primary sources and are peripheral to the switcher anatomy; treat those two as unconfirmed.
verified.products: shadcn sidebar-07 (team-switcher, nav-user); Supabase Studio (OrganizationDropdown, OrgSelector, ProjectBranchSelectorTrigger, OrgCommandItem, 2026); Sentry new navigation (organizationDropdown, 2026); Stripe sandbox banner; Vercel plan-based teams.
verified.tradeoff: Good: gives you the slots for latchkey's role (owner/admin/member/viewer as the secondary line or a badge), tripline's environment (coloured branch-style indicator), and a 'Platform' / 'All organizations' affordance for staff; the trailing Check and the InfoTip for suspended tenants are cheap, high-signal; keeping identity in the footer avoids a 5-line mega-trigger. Bad: every extra line or badge widens the minimum sidebar width and disappears entirely in the 48px rail, so the same information must be repeated in the page action bar breadcrumbs; badges on the trigger (usage, sandbox) are easy to over-use and start competing with alerts; feature-flag-gated create items mean the menu shape varies per user, which needs empty-state copy ('No organizations found') and a stable escape hatch ('All Organizations') so the list never dead-ends.

verified.name: Breadcrumb scope switcher + "projects as filters" (team ▸ project chips in the top bar, same sidebar at both levels)
verified.what: Docs name the control a "team switcher" / "scope switcher" at the top-left of the nav bar that shows teams and projects (with project avatars, a paused icon, and 'create team'); they do not explicitly describe it as separate per-level chips each with its own dropdown, nor document a deployment-level chip. The rest (sidebar consistent across team/project levels, projects-as-filters one-click switching, top-right Find, path-based scope with the ~ placeholder and d?to= resolver, default team setting) is stated verbatim in primary sources.
verified.products: Vercel dashboard — universal search 2025-06-23; new navigation opt-in 2026-01-22, default for all users 2026-02-26 (docs last updated 2026-08).
verified.tradeoff: Good: no stacked switchers — one compound control reads as the current location and supports switching either level; 'projects as filters' means you never lose the page you were on when you change project; scope in the path makes every link shareable and role-checkable. Bad: only works if page taxonomies really line up at both levels (Vercel had to unify the tabs first); a third level (environment) does not fit naturally in the breadcrumb and Vercel keeps environment as an in-page filter; breadcrumb chips get cramped in a 240px sidebar header, and at a 48px rail they collapse to avatars only.

verified.name: Account picker that also owns the environment (Stripe account ▸ sandbox), with a full-width mode banner
verified.what: Account picker (current account name, upper-left) is the scope control: its menu lists accounts, 'New account', 'Settings', and 'Switch to sandbox' (select a sandbox, 'Create sandbox', 'Manage sandboxes'; the /sandboxes overview page is an alternative entry). Opening a sandbox shows "a banner at the top of the Dashboard" (width/style unspecified) and you can navigate anywhere; you exit "with the account picker". Organizations sit above accounts with their own dashboard at /org/dashboard (reports, team, SSO, Sigma). Sandbox access levels Private/Developer/All team members and sandbox-only invites confirmed. Test mode sandbox shares settings with live; many pages show a notification box and disable live settings. Whether the action bar carries any environment control is not documented.
verified.products: Stripe Dashboard — Sandboxes (general sandboxes replacing the test-mode toggle; docs current 2026), Organizations.
verified.tradeoff: Good: one control, two axes, no second switcher; the banner makes the dangerous axis (which environment am I writing to?) impossible to miss; per-environment membership is a clean analogue for latchkey tenants and tripline environments with different roles. Bad: environment is not in the URL, so links are ambiguous across live/sandbox and the dashboard has to remember mode server-side; a submenu inside a menu hides the environment two clicks deep; the 'shared settings' caveat shows how confusing it gets when an environment is not fully isolated.

verified.name: Resource picker dialog: search + Recent / Starred / All (org ▸ folder ▸ project tree), environment badges, scope in a query param
verified.what: Google Cloud console project picker (top-of-page button) opens a dialog with an organization drop-down and Recent / All tabs over the org ▸ folder ▸ project tree, including a "No organization" bucket; capped at 4,000 resources with fallback to the Manage resources page filtered by name. Projects tagged environment=prod/dev/test/staging get a Prod/Dev/Test/Staging badge in the picker (most specific tag wins; requires Tag Viewer role) "to remind you that any changes could affect your associated production or non-production applications". Console URLs carry ?project=<id>, with project=_ used in docs deep links. Unverified by the cited primary docs: the Starred tab, a resource search box, and org/folder selection re-scoping org-level pages.
verified.products: Google Cloud console (project picker; Manage resources page; environment tag badges) — docs current 2026.
verified.tradeoff: Good: scales to thousands of scopes across a tree; recents + starred cover the common case, search covers the rest; badges bring environment awareness without a third control; org-level and project-level pages share one picker. Bad: it is a modal, so switching is a heavier interaction than a dropdown and breaks flow; users routinely land on the wrong project because the org level is invisible once inside a project; a ?project= query param is easy to drop when hand-editing links, and pages that are org-scoped still show the picker, which is confusing.

verified.name: Identity/role switch with colour-coded session label, recent roles, and per-session URLs (AWS)
verified.what: Two small tightenings: the multi-session hostname is documented as an account-ID plus opaque suffix subdomain (e.g. 000000000000-aaaaaaaa.us-east-1.console.aws.amazon.com), not explicitly a 'hash'; and the 'pick account + permission set in the access portal' detail is stated in the IAM switch-role doc's note (and the portal page's 'find the AWS accounts and applications they're authorized to access'), not as a step-by-step in the cited using-the-portal page. Also note switch-role in multi-session mode is reached via 'Add session' > 'Switch role'.
verified.products: AWS Management Console — Switch role (long-standing), multi-session console (opt-in), IAM Identity Center access portal; docs current 2026.
verified.tradeoff: Good: makes 'who am I acting as, in which account' impossible to miss via colour + label; a remembered list of recent roles makes repeated switching cheap; per-session hostnames keep tabs from clobbering each other. Bad: the switch form is manual and clunky for first use; role and account are conflated into one switch; no hierarchy (no org tree), so it does not help pick among many accounts; colour and name are user-chosen, so they are not consistent across people.

verified.name: Context-scoped sidebar: the sidebar's contents change with the scope level, drill-down instead of a second switcher (Cloudflare account ▸ zone; GitLab group ▸ project)
verified.what: Context-scoped sidebar confirmed for both. Cloudflare: sidebar lists account-level products until a zone is picked, then zone-level products; change zone via the forward arrow next to the zone name or by returning to account home; account-level access from within a zone is via an "Accounts" sidebar option (docs don't describe it as a switcher pinned at the top). Docs deep-link with ?to=/:account/:zone/... placeholders (resolution behavior not documented on the cited pages). GitLab: sidebar content depends on context (project / group / Your work / Explore / profile), pins are per-context, Admin lives in the upper-right, and context switching uses "Search or go to" (/) with : > @ ~ prefixes and frequently visited projects listed first; the docs cited do not explicitly state that the sidebar header shows the current group/project name.
verified.products: Cloudflare dashboard (accounts and zones; deep links) — docs current 2026. GitLab left sidebar redesign 16.0 (May 2023), 'Search or go to' command palette — docs current.
verified.tradeoff: Good: avoids two stacked switchers by making the second level a navigation step; the sidebar visibly tells you which level you are at because its items differ; deep-link placeholders let docs/alerts link into a scope-less path and have the shell ask for the missing scope. Bad: switching between siblings at the second level costs 2+ clicks (up to home, pick again) unless a search/command palette is added — GitLab effectively relies on it; per-context pins and per-level nav mean users must relearn the sidebar when the scope changes; with a 48px rail there is no room to show the current zone/project name, so the current scope becomes invisible when collapsed.

verified.name: Org in the icon rail + project/environment as a page-filter bar in the URL (Sentry; Datadog as the account-menu variant)
verified.what: Org in the icon rail + project/environment as a page-filter bar in the URL (Sentry; Datadog as the account-menu variant). Sentry: avatar button in the primary nav rail opens a menu with org avatar/name/'N Projects', access-gated org links, and a 'Switch Organization' submenu (active/inactive orgs + Create organization); switching is a plain link to /organizations/<slug>/issues/ (or the org's customer domain under multi-region). Page filters are not reset explicitly — they are persisted per org under localStorage key global-selection[:<namespace>]:<orgSlug> (projects, environments, dates, utc, pinnedFilters), so each org keeps its own last-used selection. Project/environment/date live in a page-filter bar mirrored to ?project=&environment=&statsPeriod= (or start/end/utc); no project param = My Projects (-2), project=-1 = All Projects; custom multi-select capped at 50; environment list derived from selected projects; forceProject/shouldForceProject for single-project pages and storageNamespace for dashboards. Datadog: org switched from the account menu; org is session context, so cross-org links 404 unless custom sub-domains (enabled by support) automatically switch context.
verified.products: Sentry (new primary navigation, 2025; page filters, current master 2026-09). Datadog (multi-org accounts, custom sub-domains; docs current).
verified.tradeoff: Good: the org control is tiny and survives the collapsed rail; project/environment as filters means one page serves any breadth (one project, several, all) and issue links carry their filters; per-org persistence plus reset-on-org-switch avoids stale cross-org state; 'My Projects' default keeps big orgs usable. Bad: three visible controls in the action bar cost horizontal space and can be mistaken for search filters rather than scope; environment values are only as good as the tags coming in; session-bound org (Datadog) breaks shared links and needs subdomain plumbing to fix; a switcher submenu hides sibling orgs two levels deep with no search, which does not scale past ~20 orgs (platform staff will need a searchable list instead).

verified.name: Keyboard switching: positional Mod+N vs chord vs command-palette picker
verified.what: Slack: the "shown on hover" wording is from the Mac page; the Windows/Linux page says the assigned number is shown under the workspace icon in the left sidebar. Sentry: both the ⌘K action and the sidebar submenu are hidden when singleOrganization OR demo mode is active, not singleOrganization alone. Grafana: condition is `orgs?.length <= 1` (also returns children when orgs is undefined).
verified.products: Slack desktop (help centre, 2026), Notion desktop (help centre, 2026), Linear (docs, 2026), Sentry (master, static/app/components/commandPalette, 2026-09), Grafana (main, AppChrome/OrganizationSwitcher, 2026-09), shadcn/ui v4 sidebar-07 block.
verified.tradeoff: Positional Mod+N is fastest for a stable short list but the mapping shifts whenever the list is reordered or an org is added, and in a browser Cmd/Ctrl+1–9 are already tab-switch shortcuts, so Slack/Notion only do this in their desktop apps. A chord (Linear's O W) and a palette entry (Sentry) are browser-safe and scale to many orgs because you type to filter; the palette also fits platform staff who can see every org. A chord needs discoverability (show it in the switcher trigger tooltip / row). Hide the whole affordance when the user has one org.

verified.name: Searchable picker with recents, favourites and status partitioning
verified.what: The per-product details are accurate, but the headline overreaches: only Postman (search field) and Grafana (Select combobox) show a searchable/filterable body. Sentry's dropdown is a plain menu partitioned into active/inactive groups with no search in the cited file; AWS's control is a manual account+role entry form plus a short cookie-backed recents list; Azure's Directories view is a Settings pane (with favourites and Switch buttons), not a header switcher. Better statement: "Switchers add search (Postman, Grafana), recents (Postman, AWS), favourites (Azure, Postman starred) or status partitioning (Sentry) individually; no single cited product combines all of these, and the 'filterable list once org count grows' rule is inferred, not documented."
verified.products: Postman (Learning Center, 2026), Azure portal (Learn, doc dated 2026-04-06), AWS IAM console (User Guide, 2026), Sentry (master, 2026-09), Grafana (main, 2026-09).
verified.tradeoff: Search plus recents covers both the two-org user and platform staff in latchkey who can see every tenant; favourites need a server-side per-user store (Azure) whereas recents can live in localStorage per device (AWS-style cookie) at the cost of not following the user across devices. Partitioning by membership status (active / suspended / invited) in the list, as Sentry does, lets the same list carry pending invitations without a separate screen. Costs: the list must be fetched on open (or cached), typeahead needs a Command/cmdk-style input that also works in the 48px rail (open as a popover anchored to the rail icon), and recents must be pruned when membership is revoked.

verified.name: URL as source of truth, session as fallback (vs server-side 'current org')
verified.what: Minor precision: Sentry's client-side fallback order is params.orgId || configStore.lastOrganization ?? organizations[0]?.slug (a persisted 'last org' preference, not a session per se), and in DEPLOY_PREVIEW mode it skips the URL param entirely. Sentry's server also only reads the URL when the caller passes an explicit organization_slug; otherwise the session is primary. Datadog's URL-driven switching is via custom subdomain (host), not a path segment. The Vercel /[team]/~/settings route was not verified against a primary source.
verified.products: Clerk (Next.js middleware docs, 2026), Sentry (master: src/sentry/web/frontend/base.py, static/app/views/organizationContext.tsx, 2026-09), Datadog (docs, 2026), Vercel (docs, updated 2026-08-28), Grafana (HTTP API docs + main, 2026-09).
verified.tradeoff: URL-scoped orgs (/o/:org) make links shareable, multi-tab safe and cacheable per route, and let a tripline alert link or a latchkey invite link land directly in the right tenant; the session/last-org value then only decides where `/` redirects. Costs: every API call must carry the org (path or header) rather than relying on session, and a URL for an org the user no longer belongs to needs an explicit not-a-member state (Clerk's docs don't define one; Sentry silently falls back to the first org, which can be confusing). Server-side current-org (Grafana) is simpler for auth gateways but breaks with two orgs open in two tabs. Subdomain-per-org (Sentry customer domains, Datadog) forces full-page navigation on switch and complicates cookie scoping.

verified.name: Remembering the landing org: explicit default (account) vs last-visited (session/device)
verified.what: Minor: Vercel's docs say the setting lives under Account Settings > "Default Team" at vercel.com/account/settings (not a separate "Default Team" settings page); Sentry's server-side fallback to the first accessible org happens in base.py when activeorg is invalid, in addition to the client-side organizations[0] fallback; AWS docs confirm cookies store role names but do not state the exact count ("last several roles").
verified.products: Vercel (docs, 2026-08-28), Azure portal (Learn, 2026-04-06), Sentry (master, 2026-09), Grafana (HTTP API, 2026), AWS IAM console (2026), Slack desktop (2026).
verified.tradeoff: A per-account default (Vercel/Azure 'Select a directory') is predictable and shareable across devices and works for CLI/API defaults; last-visited (Azure default mode, Sentry session) matches what people actually do but surprises when you switch devices or when the last org was one you were only visiting as platform staff. Server-side last-org (Grafana) is one write per switch and must be ignored when the URL already names an org. For latchkey's passwordless sign-in across three consoles, an account-level default org plus per-console last-visited (stored server-side per user+console, or in localStorage as a fallback) is the combination these products converge on; auto-reassign the default when membership is removed, as Vercel does.

verified.name: Switch semantics: land on org home vs rewrite current path; client navigation vs full reload
verified.what: Two small overstatements: (1) Sentry resolveRoute returns `${sentryUrl}${route}` built from ConfigStore links.sentryUrl (via localizeDomain) — an absolute URL in practice, but the code does not itself hard-code an `https://` prefix; (2) Sentry's org-change reset also clears PageFiltersStore, not only OrganizationStore/ProjectsStore/TeamStore. Grafana's stated rationale ("re-bootstraps cleanly") is inferred; the code comment only says the abort is "so we don't reload into the wrong org".
verified.products: Grafana (main, 2026-09), Sentry (master, 2026-09: organizationDropdown.tsx, commandPaletteGlobalActions.tsx, organizationContext.tsx, resolveRoute.tsx), Clerk (OrganizationSwitcher / OrganizationList docs, 2026), Vercel (docs, 2026-08-28), Notion (help, 2026).
verified.tradeoff: Preserving the page is only safe for org-level routes; sub-scopes (tripline project/environment, runsheet team/service, latchkey tenant) don't map across orgs, so rewrite-in-place needs a route-level rule: keep the route if it is org-scoped only, otherwise land on the org home. Client navigation keeps the shell, sidebar state and rail collapse intact but requires invalidating every org-keyed query and store (Sentry's explicit resets); a full reload (Grafana) is the cheap way to guarantee no cross-org data leaks, which matters for an identity product, at the cost of a flash and lost in-progress state. Sentry shows one product can do both: home-landing from the sidebar, page-preserving from the palette. Do the server-side switch first and abort on failure before navigating.

verified.name: Pending invitations and org creation inside the switcher
verified.what: Clerk's <OrganizationSwitcher /> shows the active org, the org list, an optional Personal Account (hidePersonal), a Manage entry and a "Create organization" button (createOrganizationMode 'modal' | 'navigation', default 'modal'; createOrganizationUrl for navigation; afterCreateOrganizationUrl for post-create routing). For verified-domain automatic invitations the user "will see a notification on the component and also receive an email" and gets a Join button next to the org; suggestions render a Request to join button. skipInvitationScreen is a prop of the separate <CreateOrganization /> component (and openCreateOrganization), not of the switcher itself. Sentry: 'Create a new organization' (IconAdd) is the last item of the Switch Organization submenu, hidden without the organizations:create feature, and an external link to the control-silo sentryUrl + /organizations/new/ under system:multi-region. Vercel: team switcher top-left > create a new team > name it > choose a plan.
verified.products: Clerk (OrganizationSwitcher, verified-domains and invitations docs, 2026), Sentry (master, 2026-09), Vercel (docs, 2026-08-28), Notion (help, 2026), Linear (docs, 2026), shadcn/ui v4 sidebar-07, GitHub (docs, 2026).
verified.tradeoff: Surfacing invitations in the switcher (Clerk) means the switcher is the one place a multi-org passwordless user discovers and accepts access, and the badge count can sit on the 48px rail avatar; it costs an extra invitations query on shell load and a rule for which surface wins when the invite was opened from email while already signed in (Clerk sends to the homepage; better to deep-link into the invited org). Email-only acceptance (GitHub) is simpler and auditable but leaves the switcher unaware. Creating an org from the switcher as a modal keeps the current page and is right for a one-field form; a navigation flow is needed when creation has multiple steps (Vercel's plan choice) or must happen on another domain (Sentry multi-region). Gate 'Create organization' by capability (Sentry's feature flag) and, for latchkey, by role — members/viewers in an org may still create their own org, but platform staff creating tenants is a different flow.

verified.name: Org trigger + sectioned popover (Clerk OrganizationSwitcher anatomy)

verified.name: Full-page tenant/realm directory with 'Current' badge, recents and favourites (for many orgs / platform staff)
verified.what: Keycloak 26 admin console: left-nav section title is the realm display name followed by a blue PatternFly Label 'Current realm'; a 'Manage realms' nav item (rendered only when the current realm is the master realm) opens a realm table with a grey 'Current realm' Badge on the active row, a 'Create realm' button, a 'Recent realms' dropdown shown only once >=3 realms have been visited (localStorage, max 3), a toolbar kebab for bulk delete of selected rows (not a per-row kebab), and since 26.7 search also matches display name. Each realm has its own dedicated admin console; nav items are filtered via hasAccess() on route access roles. Azure portal and Auth0 Teams claims are accurate as stated.
verified.products: Keycloak 26.1–26.7 admin console (Manage realms page; display-name search in 26.7); Azure portal / Microsoft Entra admin center (2026 docs); Auth0 Teams Dashboard (2025-26).
verified.tradeoff: Good: scales to hundreds of tenants; a 'Current' badge and recents/favourites give fast return paths; visibility and entry can be separated (Auth0 Teams) so staff can see every org without silently having admin rights; the sidebar label + badge pattern works unchanged in a collapsed rail (tooltip). Bad: a page navigation is heavier than a popover for the common 2–3-org user; Azure buries the switcher two clicks deep in settings which users routinely fail to find; Keycloak's model makes 'which realm am I in' depend on reading a label rather than a distinct chrome colour, and the master-realm-only 'Manage realms' item means non-staff never get a switcher at all.

verified.name: Staff access to any tenant as a time-boxed, justified, tenant-approved elevation (not a global 'god mode' toggle)
verified.what: Staff/partner access to a tenant as a time-boxed, justified, often tenant-approved elevation rather than a permanent all-orgs mode. Okta: customer admin uses Settings > Account > "Give Access to Okta Support" to "Grant impersonation for a case" (read-only admin access, 24 hours) or to "Approve" Support's self-assigned case access. Entra PIM: "My roles" lists eligible roles; "Activate" requires MFA ("Additional verification required"), optional reduced "Scope", optional custom start time, and a "Reason"; approval-gated roles show a pending notification and appear in "My requests" with a "Request Status" column; active roles show "Deactivate", not usable within five minutes of activation. GDAP: partner requests an admin relationship with a name, specific Entra roles, and "Duration in days" after which it automatically expires unless "Auto Extend" is Yes; the customer must accept. WorkOS: impersonation must be enabled per environment by an Admin, a reason is required and recorded on session.created, sessions expire after 60 minutes, and staff must pick the organization when the user belongs to several. Auth0 Teams: owners can list all tenants but cannot open tenants they are not administrators of. Drop Auth0 "Elevated Support Access" — it is a customer dashboard role for managing support tickets/usage reports, not a staff elevation mechanism.
verified.products: Okta Admin Console (Settings > Account, 2025-26 docs); Microsoft Entra PIM (2026 docs); Microsoft Partner Center GDAP (2024-26); WorkOS AuthKit impersonation (2025-26); Auth0 dashboard roles / Teams (2025-26).
verified.tradeoff: Good: makes 'platform staff can see every org' auditable and reversible; the activation form (reason + duration) doubles as the UI moment where you can switch chrome to a staff/elevated state; tenant admins can see and revoke who is inside. Bad: heavy for routine support (extra click + reason every time); apps that cache role claims may lag activation/deactivation (Microsoft explicitly warns to sign out/in); if elevation is per tenant, the org switcher for staff needs two lists (orgs I belong to vs orgs I can elevate into) which none of these products render in a single control.

verified.name: Acting-as chrome with an explicit exit (impersonation frame / floating badge, 'act' claim)
verified.what: Minor overreaches: (1) WorkOS `impersonator {email, reason}` is documented on the `session.created` webhook event (and the authenticate response per API docs), not solely the authenticate response; (2) Clerk's FAB is not literally "white"—the source uses theme tokens (icon colored t.colors.$white); the pill background comes from theme, so drop the color claim; (3) Keycloak's logout-and-swap applies only when admin and user are in the same realm—cross-realm impersonation keeps the admin logged in and additionally logs in as the user in the other realm; in both cases the user's Account Console is shown with no admin chrome or exit control documented.
verified.products: WorkOS AuthKit + authkit-nextjs Impersonation component (2025-26); Clerk ImpersonationFab (source main, Sept 2026); Descope User Impersonation (2025-26); Keycloak admin console impersonation (26.x).
verified.tradeoff: Good: a frame or FAB is visible on every page including scrolled and collapsed-sidebar states; naming the target and providing 'Stop' prevents accidental writes as the wrong principal; claims-based detection (`act`) lets every console in a shared shell render the same chrome. Bad: a floating pill (Clerk) can be dragged out of the way and forgotten and only reveals the identity on hover; a full-width frame (WorkOS) eats vertical space in a console with a sticky action bar; Keycloak's session replacement is the failure mode to avoid — no indicator, no return path; all of these are for user impersonation, none show a lighter 'viewing tenant X as staff, not as a member' state, which the latchkey shell needs as a distinct, less alarming variant.

verified.name: Personal account as a peer of organisations, with role carried in the session and nav filtered by it (not badged)
verified.what: Personal account as a peer of organisations is a product setting (Clerk 'Membership optional'; Auth0 'Both'), and the active org's role rides in the token and shapes nav in WorkOS/Clerk. Overstatements: (1) in Clerk the personal account is not literally 'the first row' of a list — it occupies the header/active slot only when no org is active (or the trigger fallback); (2) role-in-token is true for Clerk (org_role) and WorkOS, but Auth0's org_id claim identifies the org only — role is not a default claim and needs an Action to add; (3) Clerk's role IS visibly labelled (once, under the active org in the popover), so 'not badged' applies to the admin consoles (Auth0/Keycloak/FusionAuth), not to Clerk's switcher.
verified.products: Clerk Organizations + OrganizationSwitcher (2025-26); Auth0 Organizations login flows (2025-26); WorkOS AuthKit sessions + Dashboard members (2025-26); Descope Tenant Select component (2025-26); Auth0 dashboard roles; Keycloak 26 admin console; FusionAuth 1.5x admin UI.
verified.tradeoff: Good: treating personal and org as peers in one list keeps a single mental model and one control; carrying role/permissions in the session lets the shell decide what to render before the org data loads; hiding nav by role avoids 'you are a Viewer' labels that users ignore. Bad: a personal row in a B2B admin console is noise (every vendor here recommends turning it off); when nav is filtered silently, members cannot tell whether a page is missing because of role or because the feature is off — Clerk is the only one that prints the role name, and only inside the popover; the hosted org picker (Auth0) and re-auth-on-switch (Auth0, WorkOS when SSO/MFA differs) mean switching can bounce the user out of your shell, so the switcher must tolerate a redirect mid-interaction.

verified.name: Menu-button switcher with menuitemradio for the current org (small N, expanded sidebar)
verified.what: Menu-button org switcher in the sidebar header: a size="lg" SidebarMenuButton trigger (32px avatar, two truncated lines, trailing ChevronsUpDown) opening a DropdownMenu side='right' align='start' with a label, one item per membership, optional ⌘[n] shortcuts, separator, and 'Add/Create' item — as shipped in shadcn sidebar-07 TeamSwitcher (label 'Teams', plain DropdownMenuItems, no radio state). Sentry's OrganizationDropdown instead uses an avatar-only trigger, a current-org header (avatar, name, '%s Projects') and a 'Switch Organization' submenu sorted by name with active/inactive partition and textValue on each item, also without checked semantics. Using DropdownMenuRadioGroup/RadioItem with aria-checked for the current org is supported by Radix/Base UI primitives and APG menu-button keyboard semantics, but is a recommended enhancement rather than something the cited products ship.
verified.products: shadcn/ui v4 sidebar-07 'TeamSwitcher' block (2024–2026; v4 DropdownMenu is Base UI-backed with `render` prop); Radix Primitives DropdownMenu (RadioGroup/RadioItem/ItemIndicator, onCloseAutoFocus); Base UI Menu (RadioItem, finalFocus, modal); Sentry new navigation OrganizationDropdown (master, 2026) — avatar trigger, current-org header, 'Switch Organization' submenu sorted by name, active vs inactive orgs partitioned with an InfoTip on inactive ones; GitHub 'Switch dashboard context' menu (top-left username dropdown listing orgs); Linear workspace name dropdown → 'Switch workspace' submenu (also 'O then W' shortcut); Vercel team switcher at top-left of the nav bar (docs updated 2026-08).
verified.tradeoff: Good: lightest primitive, already in the shell (shadcn DropdownMenu), APG-conformant keyboard model for free, typeahead covers ~5–15 orgs, and menuitemradio gives a native way to announce 'current'. Bad: menus are for actions, not filtering — no search field (a text input inside role=menu breaks arrow-key/typeahead), items cannot contain interactive children (React Aria: 'Interactive elements within menu items are not allowed'), so 'Accept'/'Decline' buttons on an invitation row cannot live here — invitations must be a single item that navigates. Submenus (Sentry style) hide the org list one hover/ArrowRight away and are awkward on touch. Falls over above ~20 orgs and for latchkey platform staff who can see every org.

verified.name: Searchable select-only combobox in a popover (input inside the popup, virtualised) for 50+ orgs and platform staff
verified.what: Overstatements to trim: (1) The Google Cloud docs cited only confirm tag badges in the project picker; search and tabbed lists are not documented on that page. (2) The Sentry command-palette org-switching claim and the React Aria "5,000+ items" figure were not verified against a primary source and should be dropped or sourced. (3) In Base UI's input-inside-popup variant the trigger is a Combobox.Trigger button, not itself role=combobox; the role=combobox/aria-activedescendant semantics apply to the input inside the popup (APG's select-only example puts role=combobox on the trigger only when there is no text input). (4) cmdk's own text says shouldFilter={false} is for manual filtering with better performance, not a hard requirement "beyond" 2,000–3,000 items.
verified.products: Base UI Combobox (2025–2026; searchable-select variant, useFilter, Combobox.Status/Empty, virtualization example); shadcn/ui v4 Combobox (Base UI-based, ComboboxEmpty) and the older Popover+Command (cmdk v1) recipe; GitHub Primer SelectPanel (React, used for GitHub's repo/label/assignee pickers; loading spinner, 'No items available', focusOutBehavior, fullscreen on narrow); Google Cloud console project picker (search, tabbed lists, tag badges as visual indicators); Sentry's command palette also lists org switching as a global action.
verified.tradeoff: Good: the only pattern that scales to latchkey platform staff (every org) and to 50+ memberships; aria-activedescendant keeps focus in the input so users type and arrow in one gesture; live-region status covers async loading and result counts; APG explicitly recommends combobox when 'the value must be one of a predefined set of allowed values'. Bad: heavier (search state, async fetch, virtualiser); virtualised rows break Ctrl+F and aria-setsize/posinset need care; grouping + virtualisation is fiddly; opening focuses the input, so keyboard users must ArrowDown to hear the current org — put the current org first or mark it aria-selected and announce it in the trigger's name; the empty-collection state needs `allowsEmptyCollection`/Combobox.Empty so the popup does not silently collapse. Overkill for members of 1–5 orgs, so many products (Sentry, Linear) keep a plain menu and add search only in a separate 'all organizations' page.

verified.name: Collapsed 48px icon rail: avatar-only trigger with tooltip and a persistent accessible name
verified.what: Collapsed 48px icon rail: shadcn's SidebarMenuButton in collapsible="icon" mode shrinks to size-8 (lg: p-0) with text hidden, and its `tooltip` prop renders a right-side TooltipContent hidden unless state==="collapsed" and not mobile. Sentry's rail trigger is an AvatarButton with aria-label "Toggle organization menu" (no org name). Slack's rail supports Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+S to expand/collapse, Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab to cycle, Cmd/Ctrl+[n] to jump; the assigned number appears on hover on Mac and under the icon on Windows/Linux. Base UI requires an aria-label on the trigger matching the tooltip and disables tooltips on touch; Radix opens the tooltip on Tab without delay and closes on Enter/Space/Esc. Recommendations (aria-label including org name + purpose, ArrowDown opening the menu, focus return on Esc, distinct initials avatars, invite badge) are design guidance, not documented behavior of these products.
verified.products: shadcn/ui v4 Sidebar (2024–2026) — SidebarMenuButton `tooltip` prop, icon collapsible mode, SidebarRail with aria-label 'Toggle Sidebar' and tabIndex=-1, Cmd/Ctrl+B toggle; Sentry new navigation (2025–2026) — icon rail with AvatarButton org trigger; Slack desktop workspace switcher rail (long-standing; help article on multiple workspaces); Radix Tooltip; Base UI Tooltip.
verified.tradeoff: Good: preserves the switcher in 48px without a second component; tooltip restores the name for mouse/keyboard users; shortcuts (Cmd+[n]) make switching faster than in the expanded state. Bad: avatar-only identity is weak when several orgs share initials or have no logo; tooltips do not exist on touch and are not reliably announced, so the aria-label must carry the org name and role; two right-anchored popups (tooltip, then menu) can stack — close the tooltip on open (Radix does on Enter/Space) and disable it while the menu is open; the role/tenant second line disappears entirely, so role-dependent affordances need another cue (e.g. a 'Viewer' lock icon overlay or the role restated inside the popup header).

verified.name: Cardinality states: zero orgs → full-page chooser/create gate; one org → identity without a 'switch' affordance; invitations and inactive orgs listed inline
verified.what: Zero orgs: Sentry sets OrganizationStore.setNoOrganization() when no org resolves and its login redirect (sentry/utils/auth.py get_org_redirect_url) sends users to /organizations/new/; Clerk's OrganizationList is the documented post-sign-in choose-or-create screen listing memberships, automatic invitations and suggestions with afterSelectOrganizationUrl/afterCreateOrganizationUrl; Auth0 asks new accounts to create a tenant. Creation gating: Sentry hides 'Create a new organization' in the dropdown unless the organizations:create feature is on; the zero-org 'ask an admin' copy is a latchkey design decision, not a sourced pattern. One org: Sentry hides the 'Switch Organization' submenu via a deployment-wide singleOrganization config flag (not a per-user membership count) while keeping the org header and settings links; applying this per-user is an extrapolation. Clerk docs do not describe zero/one-org switcher rendering; hidePersonal only removes the Personal Account entry. Many orgs: Sentry partitions active vs inactive (org.status.id === 'active'), sorts each by name via lodash orderBy, marks inactive items with an InfoTip showing status.name, and each item navigates via `to: /organizations/{slug}/issues/`; Clerk navigates via afterSelectOrganizationUrl. Invitation count badge on the trigger and role-as-description text are unsourced proposals.
verified.products: Clerk OrganizationSwitcher + OrganizationList (2024–2026: hidePersonal, skipInvitationScreen, createOrganizationMode modal|navigation, afterSelect/afterCreate URLs); Sentry (2026 master: singleOrganization flag, organizations:create feature, active/inactive partition, no-organization state); Auth0 dashboard tenant creation on first sign-up; Vercel (default team chosen on login; team switcher top-left; create team from the switcher); Linear ('Create or join a workspace' under Switch workspace).
verified.tradeoff: Good: avoids the classic bugs — a switcher with one radio item, a 'Create' item shown to viewers who cannot create, and invitations buried in email; the full-page zero-state also solves focus management (nothing to trap). Bad: hiding the switch affordance for single-org users hides the path to a second org — keep 'Invitations' and (if allowed) 'Create organization' reachable from the identity menu or account menu; per-console scope (project/env, team/service, tenant) must be reset on switch and the breadcrumb re-rooted, which most switcher libraries do not handle; invitation Accept/Decline needs dialog or page semantics (not menu items), so either navigate to an invitations page or use the bottom-sheet/dialog variant.

verified.name: Loading, switching and privileged-access states with live-region announcements
verified.what: Primer's loading pattern specifies <1s show nothing, 1–3s indeterminate indicator, one announcement per skeleton group, and aria-busy on live regions during updates; Primer SelectPanel exposes a `loading` spinner prop, a default "No items available" empty message (used for both empty and no-match), and guidelines show a "Failed to load results" error placeholder with retry. Primer ActionList accessibility says a screen reader should announce when filtering completes (it does not specifically mandate announcing a result count). cmdk documents Command.Loading for async loading; Base UI Combobox.Status is an aria-live status message component. Sentry's organizationContext.tsx resets Organization/Projects/Team/PageFilters stores and calls switchOrganization() on slug change, measures a 'ui.bootstrap' span, and opens a non-closable sudo modal for superusers on 403 — and for superuser+staff users when the org's access array is empty. The 'Switched to Acme Corp' announcement, 'Staff view' badge, and retry-vs-no-results distinction are the author's design proposals rather than documented patterns.
verified.products: GitHub Primer loading pattern + SelectPanel loading/empty states (2024–2026); Base UI Combobox.Status (2025–2026); cmdk Command.Loading; Sentry organizationContext (2026 master: store resets, ui.bootstrap span, superuser sudo modal, staff sessions); shadcn Skeleton in sidebar (SidebarMenuSkeleton); Slack/Notion/Linear numeric and chorded switch shortcuts.
verified.tradeoff: Good: prevents the two worst regressions — layout shift in the sidebar header while the session loads, and silent context switches for screen-reader users; separates 'no orgs', 'no matches', 'failed to load' and 'not permitted' so support can tell them apart. Bad: live regions are easy to over-fire (announce once per switch, not per store reset); aria-busy on a region suppresses announcements until cleared, so a stuck loading state goes silent; full-page bootstrap on switch is slower than in-place data swapping but is what keeps URLs, breadcrumbs and per-console scopes consistent; staff/superuser modes add a third role dimension that the role badge in the switcher has to represent.
